18th April, 1941. 


Dear Mr. Sharman, 


I should be grateful if you would cause 
enquiries to be made as to the present whereabouts 
of Mr. Harold Owen Thorpe, a British subject, who 
is supposed to have left Yokohama,as a seaman, 
in September 1940, and believed to be in Shanghai. 
He was last registered here in 1939 when he gave 
his address as 5 Yang Terrace, Weihaiwei Road. 


I should also be greteful for any information 
as to the whereabouts of his brother, Bruce Arthur 
Thorpe, and his wife, who are supposed to have 
returned to their home in Shanghai. Their last 
address in Shanghai being given as c/o Shanghai 
Telephone Company, or 9 Ching Yang Road, off 
Dixwell Road. 


Yours sincerely, 


V. Sharmen, Esquire, 


Assistant Commissioner, 
Shanghai Municipal Police, 
SHANGHAI.

April 26 41.

Dear Mr. Cox,

In reply to your letter dated April 18,
1941, I have to inform you that the present address
of Mr. Harold Owen Thorpe and Mr. and Mrs. Bruce
Arthur Thorpe is 163 Yuen Ching Fong, North Szechuan
Road, a boarding-house owned by their mother,
Mrs. Marie Thorpe nee Satsuke.

Yours sincerely,

E. Sharman
Assistant Commissioner
(Special Branch)

A. T. Cox, Esq.,
British Consulate-General,
Shanghai.

I should also be grateful for any information

护照与登记办公室，
英国驻上海总领事馆
邮政信箱 259 号。
上海。

1941 年 4 月 18 日。

亲爱的 Sharman 先生：

如蒙协助查询英籍人士 Harold Owen Thorpe 先生的目前下落，我将不胜感激。据信他于 1940 年 9 月以海员身份离开横滨，现被认为在上海。他最后一次在此登记是在 1939 年，当时提供的地址是威海卫路杨氏别墅 5 号。

此外，如能提供其兄弟 Bruce Arthur Thorpe 及其妻子的下落信息，我也将不胜感激，据信他们已返回上海的住所。他们在上海的最后地址记载为转交上海电话公司，或狄思威路附近的静安路 9 号。

此致

敬礼

V. Sharman 先生，
助理总监，
上海公共租界工部局警务处，
上海。
